g.text: An address swap and an item change through the J++ lens, against 200 random vectors of the same size
Grey strip: 200 random vectors of the same norm, read the same way; the strip is where 95% of them land (z is
centred on their median, so each row's own 95% range sits within 0.19 of the strip's edges).
Left: z = (ln m − ln r) / w, with r the median rank over the cases of the new item's name (item change) or of
the best-ranked of 15 position words such as first, next, 2 (address swap), m the random vectors' median of
the same, w half their 95% range of ln rank.
Right: z = (share − m) / w, with m the random vectors' median share and w half their 95% range. The swap's
share against that median: 0.06 / 0.05 (9B); 0.04 / 0.04 (27B); 0.01 / 0.01 (Muse).
Asked to say the position, the 27B never has the right ordinal word in the lens's top five (0.00, n = 200),
yet loses 0.28 of its reports without the address (extra loss, beyond a random part).
